Through an interactive environmental time machine, it integrates historical analysis, weather forecasts, and activity planning. Users can explore environmental trends, interpret statistical charts, schedule events, find more favorable dates, and receive automatic notifications when weather conditions change.

details:
Project Description

EarthLens is an environmental and geospatial intelligence platform that enables users to investigate historical trends, access weather forecasts, and plan future activities in selected cities and regions.

The project was inspired by the climate variability of Comodoro Rivadavia, where strong winds, rainfall, and changing weather conditions can affect everyday life, tourism, and economic activities.

Functionality and Innovation

Our main innovation lies in integrating historical analysis, weather forecasts, and activity planning through an interactive environmental time machine.

Earth Time Machine allows users to travel backward and forward in time within a single interactive map, select geographical locations and time ranges, explore different environmental variables, and visualize their evolution through statistical charts.

The platform enables users to identify trends, anomalies, and changes in variables such as temperature, precipitation, atmospheric humidity, wind speed, soil moisture, and vegetation, depending on data availability.

Each city also has its own environmental profile, bringing together geographical characteristics, historical data, and environmental trends. This includes Earth Fingerprint, a graphical representation of its environmental characteristics.

Users can create personal accounts, schedule events through an integrated calendar, access weather forecasts, receive recommendations for alternative dates, and obtain automatic notifications about changing conditions that could affect their activities.

The system also enables users to store results, review historical records, and export reports for environmental research or activity planning.

Scientific Data and Methodology

EarthLens uses more than 90,000 scientific data records across 300 time series, covering 25 Argentine cities from 2000 to 2024.

The main data sources include:

  • NASA POWER: Atmospheric and meteorological variables.
  • NASA GLDAS 2.1: Soil moisture and evapotranspiration.
  • NASA GPM/IMERG V07: Satellite-based precipitation estimates.
  • NASA MODIS: Vegetation analysis, with partial integration.
  • NASA SWOT: Experimental analysis of water bodies and hydrological variables.
  • ERA5: Historical meteorological reanalysis data.
  • Open-Meteo: Daily and hourly weather forecasts.
  • GeoRef Argentina: Official geographical information and city locations.

Scientific analysis is conducted using statistical methods such as ordinary least squares (OLS) linear regression, slope estimation, p-values, and confidence intervals. These methods enable the evaluation of the direction, magnitude, and uncertainty of environmental trends.

The platform distinguishes between historical records, weather forecasts, and future estimates while acknowledging their respective limitations.

Technologies and Development Tools

EarthLens was developed using Python, Flask, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS, following a modular architecture based on services and REST APIs.

Leaflet.js was used for geographical visualization and interactive mapping, while Chart.js was used to display time series, comparative charts, and environmental profiles. SciPy was used for scientific data processing and statistical analysis.

Docker and Docker Compose were used to provide a reproducible execution environment. Git and GitHub supported version control and collaborative development, while Antigravity and Visual Studio Code were used as development environments.

Artificial intelligence tools, including ChatGPT, OpenAI Codex, Google Gemini, and Claude Opus, were also used to assist with programming, research, documentation, design, and software testing under human supervision.

Impact and Target Audience

EarthLens is primarily designed for:

  • Scientists and environmental researchers.
  • Geography and environmental science students.
  • Tourism companies.
  • Event organizers and outdoor activity planners.

Our goal is to generate educational, social, and economic impact by democratizing access to scientific data, supporting environmental research, and improving activity planning in the face of adverse weather conditions.

For scientists and students, EarthLens provides accessible tools to explore environmental changes, interpret statistical results, and better understand the relationship between environmental variables and geographical territories.

For tourism companies and event organizers, it provides tools to evaluate weather conditions, identify more favorable dates, monitor scheduled activities, and anticipate potential disruptions.

The platform aims to reduce uncertainty in decision-making by integrating information that is traditionally scattered across multiple scientific and meteorological sources.

Validation and Scalability

Throughout development, we conducted automated testing, data integrity checks, and functional interface testing, achieving 236 successful automated tests in one of our latest technical evaluations.

Although EarthLens initially focuses on Argentina, its modular, multi-provider architecture was designed to facilitate the integration of additional scientific data sources, environmental variables, cities, and regions.

This approach provides the potential for international expansion, allowing EarthLens to adapt to different geographical territories, climate conditions, and environmental challenges worldwide.

Our ultimate goal is to transform Earth observation data into accessible knowledge and practical decision-making tools, enabling people to understand the past, interpret the present, and plan for the future.

EarthLens — Understand the past. Anticipate the future.
